body:
Observed while verifying #947 on a live root-path container (the fixed build and
stock v4.1.29 behave identically, so this is pre-existing, not a regression):

    USER   COMMAND
    abc    python3 /app/calibre-web-automated/cps.py
    root   python3 .../scripts/watch_fallback.py --path .../metadata_change_logs
    root   python3 .../scripts/metadata_change_dispatch.py --watch-folder ...

metadata-change-detector/run:32 invokes watch_fallback.py with no privilege
drop, while the same unit's line 81 (cwa-as-abc inotifywait ..., after #947)
does drop. So the inotify path runs as abc and the polling fallback path runs as
root, in the same service, watching the same directory.

Two consequences: files the fallback path creates under the watch folder land
owned by root, which the abc-owned services then cannot rewrite; and it is more
privilege than the job needs.

Deliberately not folded into #947 -- that issue is the container failing to
start at all as non-root, and widening a startup fix into privilege-hygiene
changes on a path that works today would have made it riskier than it needed to
be. Wants its own change with its own before/after on ingest.
title: metadata-change-detector starts two watchers as root while its sibling drops to abc
